intro:
Obadiah, the fourth of The Twelve (Minor Prophets), is the shortest OT book—one chapter targeting Edom (descendants of Esau). When Babylon destroyed Jerusalem, Edom didn't just watch—they celebrated, looted, and handed over survivors. 'You shouldn't have gloated over your brother in the day of his misfortune.'

God's message: 'As you have done, it will be done to you.' Edom's pride ('Who can bring me down?') will be humbled. Their mountain fortresses (Petra/Sela) won't save them.

Contrast: While Edom is destroyed, Israel will be restored and possess their land. 'The kingdom will be the Lord's.'
outro: Obadiah addresses ancient sibling rivalry gone toxic—Jacob vs. Esau's descendants. The principle: gloating over others' downfall brings reciprocal judgment. Edom represents all who exploit others' crises. The book affirms that God sees national crimes and holds nations accountable. Hope remains for God's people despite betrayal by 'family.'
